short: the numbered table of names, types and literals at the front of a class file. most of the file points into it.
the per-frame stack that bytecode instructions push to and pop from. the JVM's scratchpad, next to the local variable array.
classes from one source file that may use each other's private members directly. java 11, JEP 181.
a per-class table of method pointers grouped by interface, used by invokeinterface.
a class's static initializer: static fields and static blocks, run once on first active use.
a class loader asks its parent first and only looks itself when the parent comes back empty.
running code at levels 0 to 4: interpreter, three flavours of C1, then C2, climbing as it gets hotter.
swapping a long-running loop from the interpreter into compiled code while it runs. the % in PrintCompilation.
a virtual call that has seen three or more receiver classes. C2 stops inlining it.
the exit C2 compiles in for cases its profile said never happen. hitting one deoptimizes the method.
C2 skipping an allocation entirely and keeping a non-escaping object's fields in registers.
a JDK method the JIT replaces with hand-written machine code, like System.arraycopy or Integer.bitCount.
storing references in 32 bits by shifting 8-byte-aligned addresses. works for heaps up to about 32 GB.
an 8-byte object header with the class pointer folded into the mark word. product in 25, default in 27.
HotSpot's uncontended lock: one CAS on the mark word's lock bits plus a push on the thread's lock stack.
turning a contended or waited-on lock into a full ObjectMonitor with entry and wait queues.
how long the JVM waits for every running thread to reach a poll before a global pause can start.
a JVM operation that stops just one thread at its next poll instead of all of them. java 10.
class data sharing: parsed class metadata saved to an archive and mapped in at startup.
Leyden's startup archive: classes already loaded and linked, plus method profiles, from a training run. java 24+.
